item.title: Call for registration: Creative Entrepreneurship online workshop
item.description: The South African Cultural Observatory (SACO) will host an online capacity-building workshop examining the drivers of entrepreneurial success in the cultural and creative industries (CCIs). Titled More than Just Talent – Findings & Implications from a National Study on Creative Sector Entrepreneurial Success, the session will present insights from a 2025 national study of creative entrepreneurs and explore their practical implications. item.title: Artist coalition urges music community to reject Suno AI platform
item.description: A coalition of artist representatives has published an open letter calling on the music community to reject the AI music generator Suno, citing concerns over copyright and the use of artists’ work to train generative systems. The letter, titled Say No to Suno, was published on 23 February on the Music Technology Policy blog. item.title: Google acquires ProducerAI, brings team into Labs and DeepMind
item.description: Google has acquired ProducerAI, the artificial intelligence music creation platform previously known as Riffusion, integrating the start-up and its team into Google Labs. The deal was announced on 24 February in a blog post by Elias Roman, senior director of product management at Google Labs. Roman described ProducerAI as “a creative collaborator” that enables users to “turn imagination into dynamic, comprehensive songs”. item.title: Sandy B, soFa elsewhere unveil politically charged album Forward in Reverse
item.description: South African kwaito artist Sandy B has teamed up with Belgian producer soFa elsewhere to release a politically charged album titled Forward in Reverse. The collaboration was inspired by ongoing global conflicts and reflects the artists’ shared belief that music remains a vehicle for political expression. item.title: SACEM signs landmark agreement with UAE’s first CMO
item.description: The Society of Authors, Composers, and Publishers of Music (SACEM) has signed a representation agreement with the Emirates Arts & Music Rights Association (EMRA), the first not-for-profit collective management organisation (CMO) in the United Arab Emirates. The agreement enables creators in the UAE to benefit from a structured system for collecting and distributing royalties locally and internationally for the first time. item.title: Karyn White to headline advocacy concert against GBVF in Durban
item.description: American R&B singer Karyn White will perform in Durban, South Africa on 4 April as part of the Iconic Global Advocacy Concert Against Gender-Based Violence and Femicide (GBVF). The event, taking place at the Olive Convention Centre, aims to raise awareness and mobilise support against GBVF through a combination of music, advocacy, and community engagement. item.title: SA: Black Motion remix Karmacoda’s Time for 6 March release
item.description: South African Afro-house duo Black Motion are set to release a remix of San Francisco-based duo Karmacoda’s track ‘Time’ on 6 March via Sola Musa Music. The remix follows a previously released version by Prince Kaybee. Formed in 2010, Black Motion now consists of founder Thabo Mabogwane and Kabelo “Problem Child Ten83” Koma. item.title: SA: SponchMakhekhe set to release Afro-house single Inkanuko
item.description: By Lucky Mqoboli and Nkululeko Njapa South African singer and songwriter Sponch Makhekhe is set to release his new single, ‘Inkanuko’, a track blending Afro-house and amapiano influences to explore themes of love, longing and emotional vulnerability. ‘Inkanuko’, which translates as “longing for love”, combines piano melodies, layered harmonies and textured percussion, balancing emotional depth with danceable rhythms. item.title: Nigeria: Tiwa Savage launches music foundation with Berklee College
item.description: Nigerian Afrobeats artist Tiwa Savage has launched the Tiwa Savage Music Foundation, a philanthropic initiative aimed at supporting the development of emerging African music professionals. The foundation seeks to widen access to structured training across the music industry, focusing not only on performers but also on producers, songwriters, sound engineers, executives and other creative professionals. item.title: Gxarha: Redefining SA hip hop with culture, courage and conviction
item.description: By Axolile Lucky Mke and Sibongile Kobo South African rapper Cwenga Nomnganga, known professionally as Gxarha, is rapidly making his mark on the African hip hop scene. Speaking to Music in Africa, he reflected on the significance of his name, his identity, and the community that has supported him beyond music.
